pool_config.pool_brief: Build an object-based management system for a Nigerian business context. Your solution must use: an object with at least 4 properties and 2 methods (using `this`), nested object or array access, bracket notation with a variable, destructuring, Object.entries or for...in for iteration, and a lookup table pattern. All variables must use const or let (no var).

projects.title: Konga Product Profile System
projects.scenario: Build a product profile system for a Konga seller. Model a product as an object with data, methods, and a complete display pipeline.
requirements: Create a `product` object with at least 5 properties (id, name, price, category, inStock, and a nested `specs` object with at least 2 fields)
Add a method `getLabel()` that uses `this` to return: 'Wireless Earbuds — ₦4500 [Electronics]'
Add a method `isAvailable()` that uses `this.inStock` to return true/false
Use bracket notation with a variable to dynamically access and print 3 properties
Destructure at least 3 properties from the object
Use a lookup table object to map category strings to descriptions, look up the product's category, and print the result
Use Object.entries and forEach to print all properties of the nested specs object

files.content:
Konga Product Profile System

Open the browser console to see your output.

projects.title: Publica Academy Student Record System
projects.scenario: Build a student record system for Publica Academy. Model a student as a rich object with grades, contact, module history, and display methods.
requirements: Create a `student` object with id, name, score, course, a nested `contact` object (email, city, phone), and a `modules` array with at least 3 module objects (id, title, passed)
Add a method `getGrade()` using `this.score` with early returns: Pass (>=70), Borderline (>=50), Fail
Add a method `getSummary()` that calls `this.getGrade()` and uses `this.name` and `this.score`
Use bracket notation with a variable to access 3 properties dynamically
Destructure the contact object into individual variables and print them
Use a lookup table to map grade strings to motivational messages, look up the student's grade
Use for...in to iterate the student's flat properties (skip objects and arrays using typeof)

Publica Academy Student Record

projects.title: PiggyVest Account Dashboard
projects.scenario: Build an account dashboard object for a PiggyVest user. Model the account with financial data, limits, and reporting methods.
requirements: Create an `account` object with id, owner, balance, savingsGoal, a nested `limits` object (dailyWithdrawal, monthlyTransfer), and a `transactions` array with at least 3 transaction objects
Add a method `getProgress()` that uses `this.balance` and `this.savingsGoal` to return a progress string: '₦18000 of ₦50000 (36%)'
Add a method `canWithdraw(amount)` that uses `this.balance` and `this.limits.dailyWithdrawal` to check if the withdrawal is allowed
Use bracket notation with a variable to access 3 account properties dynamically
Destructure the limits object into individual variables
Use a lookup table to map transaction types to symbols (deposit → '+', withdrawal → '-')
Use Object.entries + forEach to print all limit settings

projects.title: Paystack Merchant Profile
projects.scenario: Build a merchant profile system for a Paystack business account. Model the merchant with financial data, rates, and reporting methods.
requirements: Create a `merchant` object with id, businessName, totalRevenue, transactionCount, a nested `fees` object (processingRate, capAmount), and a `recentPayments` array with at least 3 payment objects
Add a method `getNetRevenue()` that uses `this.totalRevenue` and `this.fees.processingRate` to calculate and return revenue after fees
Add a method `getAverageTransaction()` that uses `this.totalRevenue` and `this.transactionCount` to return the average
Use bracket notation with a variable to access 3 merchant properties dynamically
Destructure the fees object into variables and print them
Use a lookup table to map business category strings to Paystack plan names
Use Object.keys on the fees object to print a formatted fee schedule

projects.title: Bolt Driver Performance Report
projects.scenario: Build a driver performance report system for a Bolt driver. Model the driver with trip history, earnings, and computed metrics.
requirements: Create a `driver` object with id, name, totalTrips, totalEarnings, rating, a nested `vehicle` object (model, plate, year), and a `recentTrips` array with at least 3 trip objects
Add a method `getNetEarnings()` that uses `this.totalEarnings` and deducts 20% Bolt commission
Add a method `getRatingBadge()` that uses `this.rating` to return 'Gold' (>=4.8), 'Silver' (>=4.5), or 'Standard'
Use bracket notation with a variable to access 3 driver properties dynamically
Destructure the vehicle object into individual variables
Use a lookup table to map rating badge strings to descriptions
Use Object.entries + forEach to print all vehicle details

descriptors.full: Object has at least 4 properties and 2 methods; methods correctly use `this` to access object properties and return computed values
descriptors.partial: Methods defined but `this` not used, or methods don't return values (only console.log)
descriptors.none: Methods missing, or `this` absent from methods, or methods produce incorrect results

descriptors.full: Bracket notation used with a variable (not a string literal) to access properties dynamically; destructuring extracts at least 3 properties correctly
descriptors.partial: One of the two techniques used correctly, the other missing or using static string instead of variable
descriptors.none: Both bracket notation with variable and destructuring missing

descriptors.full: Object.entries/for...in iterates properties correctly; lookup table maps at least 3 keys to values and is accessed dynamically with a variable
descriptors.partial: One of the two implemented correctly, the other missing or using if/else instead of lookup table
descriptors.none: Both iteration and lookup table missing

descriptors.full: const/let used correctly, method names are verbs, nested access uses correct chain syntax, output is clear and well-formatted
descriptors.none: var used, poor naming, or output is difficult to read
